construction_markdown:
Let
\[
p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1,
\qquad F=\mathbb F_2[Z]/(p),
\]
and write \(\alpha=Z\bmod p\). Identify \(a=\sum_{i=0}^{15}a_i\alpha^i\in F\) with \((a_0,\ldots,a_{15})\in\mathbb F_2^{16}\).

Define the outer evaluation set
\[
A=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^{14}u_i\alpha^i:u_i\in\mathbb F_2\right\},
\qquad |A|=2^{15}.
\]
Order it by the integer \(\sum_i u_i2^i\). The genus-zero AG outer code is
\[
C_{\rm out}=\{(f(x))_{x\in A}:f\in F[X],\ \deg f\le64\},
\]
equivalently \(C_L(D,64P_\infty)\) on \(\mathbb P^1/F\).

For \(a=\sum_{i=0}^{15}a_i\alpha^i\), define
\[
H(a)=\bigl(a_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}a_i y_i\bigr)_{y\in\mathbb F_2^{15}},
\]
with \(y\) in binary-integer order. Thus \(H:F\to\mathbb F_2^{2^{15}}\) is an explicit linear realization of \(\operatorname{RM}(1,15)\).

Finally set
\[
C=\{(H(f(x)))_{x\in A}:f\in F[X],\deg f\le64\},
\]
flattening the outer blocks in the stated order. No shortening, padding, or random choice occurs.

Since \(|g(A\setminus R)|\le32703<|F^*|\), choose \(z\notin g(A\setminus R)\). Then \(z^{-1}g\) has 65 zero blocks and never produces the all-one inner symbol, so its binary weight is only \(32703\cdot2^{14}=535805952\), below target.

distance_audit: Every nonzero outer polynomial of degree at most 64 has at most 64 zeros among the 32768 distinct evaluation points.
Every nonzero inner affine truth table has weight at least 2^14; the sole nonzero constant word has weight 2^15.
Therefore every nonzero concatenated word has weight at least (32768-64)·2^14=32704·16384=535822336.
The lower bound is attained: choose 64 fixed evaluation roots, then scale their monic root polynomial so that its remaining values avoid the field element 1, which is the all-one inner symbol.
explicitness_audit: The field polynomial is explicit. Repeated squaring gives Z^256≡Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z and Z^65536≡Z modulo p; Euclidean remainders for gcd(p,Z^256+Z) are Z^2+1 and 1, certifying irreducibility.
All field elements, evaluation points, inner coordinates, outer blocks, and flattened coordinates have specified binary-integer orderings.
There are exactly 65 unrestricted F_{2^16} message coefficients and no hidden subcode selection.
There are no floors, punctures, shortenings, repetitions, padding coordinates, searches, or random choices in the encoder.

proof_markdown:
# Genus-zero AG code with affine binary inner code

## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters
\[
[1,073,741,824,1040,535,822,336]_2.
\]
Its rate is \(1040/2^{30}=65/2^{26}\).

## Field certificate

Let \(p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1\). Direct repeated squaring modulo \(p\) gives
\[
Z^{2^8}\equiv Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z,
\qquad Z^{2^{16}}\equiv Z.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\gcd(p,Z^{2^8}+Z)=1,
\]
as Euclidean division gives successive nonzero remainders \(Z^2+1\) and \(1\). Since 2 is the only prime divisor of 16, the standard finite-field irreducibility criterion proves that \(p\) is irreducible. Hence \(F=\mathbb F_2[Z]/(p)\) is the explicitly specified field of order \(2^{16}\).

## Linearity, length, and dimension

The outer message space consists of the 65 coefficients of a polynomial \(f\in F[X]\) of degree at most 64. Evaluation on \(A\) is \(F\)-linear. If such an \(f\) vanishes at every point of \(A\), it has at least 32768 roots; the polynomial root bound forces \(f=0\). Thus the outer evaluation map is injective and has dimension 65 over \(F\).

The map \(H\) is \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear and injective: the value at \(y=0\) recovers \(a_0\), and comparison with the values at the 15 unit vectors recovers \(a_1,\ldots,a_{15}\). Consequently the composite encoder is binary linear and injective. Its dimension is therefore
\[
16\cdot65=1040.
\]
There are \(|A|=2^{15}\) outer blocks, each of length \(2^{15}\), so
\[
n=2^{15}2^{15}=2^{30}=1,073,741,824.
\]

## Minimum distance

Let \(f\ne0\) have degree at most 64. At most 64 of its 32768 evaluations vanish, so at least 32704 outer symbols are nonzero. If \(a\in F\setminus\{0,1\}\), at least one of \(a_1,\ldots,a_{15}\) is nonzero, and the associated nonconstant affine function is balanced; hence \(\operatorname{wt}(H(a))=2^{14}\). Also \(H(1)\) is the all-one word of weight \(2^{15}\). Every nonzero block therefore has weight at least \(2^{14}\), giving
\[
\operatorname{wt}(C(f))\ge32704\cdot2^{14}
=(2^{15}-2^6)2^{14}=2^{29}-2^{20}=535,822,336.
\]

This bound is attained. Fix the first 64 points \(R\subset A\) and put \(g(X)=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r)\). The set \(g(A\setminus R)\subset F^*\) has at most 32704 elements, strictly fewer than \(|F^*|=65535\). Let \(z\) be the first nonzero field element, in the specified polynomial-basis order, outside this image, and take \(f=z^{-1}g\). Then \(f\) vanishes exactly on \(R\) and never takes the value 1 on \(A\setminus R\). Its 64 zero blocks have weight zero and all remaining 32704 blocks have weight exactly \(2^{14}\). Thus the displayed lower bound is the exact minimum distance.

All choices are symbolic and deterministic, completing the proof.
